I will start from what I did last year and only adjust a little. I have 65 mu, and with 3 people in the house I cannot spread myself too thin on crops that need too much hand work, so I will keep the main land in wheat-maize and use the rest for cash crops. In Quzhou our water comes from wells, so I do not fear drought as much as dryland farmers, but electricity, fertilizer, pesticide, seed, and labor all cost real money, so I will put the heavier fertilizer on the crops that pay back fast, like cabbage, chili, and watermelon. Wheat and maize are still my base. I will not cut fertilizer too hard on grain, because if yield drops, that loss is bigger than saving a little on one bag of fertilizer. For wheat and maize, I will follow what has worked in recent years around me: stable improved or hybrid seed, enough base fertilizer, then topdressing by growth stage, and timely irrigation. For cabbage and chili, I will feed more because they take fertilizer hard and show it quickly if they are short. Watermelon needs potassium more, otherwise the fruit size and sweetness fall. Stevia I will keep on a smaller area, manage it steadily, and not overspend. Tillage-wise, I will plough before wheat and most spring cash crops, and after wheat I will do maize with less disturbance to save time and moisture. I do not gamble much at the start of the season; I do what I know can give me a safe harvest, then I adjust a little if weather or prices change.
